newsitem.title: EGYPT: Israel PM wants to complete peace deals with PLO.
newsitem.headline: Israel PM wants to complete peace deals with PLO.

text.p: Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said in remarks published on Saturday he wanted his government to be the one to make final peace with Palestinians.
"We want to be the government which completes the peace agreement in its final form with the Palestinians," he said in an interview in the Arabic language Akhbar al-Youm newspaper.
Israeli-PLO peace moves have been in crisis -since Netanyahu sent bulldozers in March to an Arab East Jerusalem hillside to build Jewish homes.
Israel's settlement policy has angered its peace partners who say the policy disregards existing peace agreements.
Asked if he had said that the Oslo peace agreement was dead, Netanyahu said: "I have never said that. I said the opposite, that we are adhering to Oslo."

But asked how he saw the final outcome, Netanyahu said: "Oslo has left out the final situation. It does not define the final shape. There is a common opinion in the Arab world that Oslo has defined the final form."
The European Union is trying to set up a meeting between Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy in Brussels on July 22 aimed at ending the crisis.
Egypt, the first Arab state to sign a peace treaty with Israel, is among mediators and its recent efforts include a package of Israeli-PLO confidence-building measures.
"The Egyptian role is a very good one, especially during the past three months. I see Egypt's efforts in the last period as just and wise," Netanyahu was quoted as saying.
He was asked in the interview about Egypt's peace process mediation bid.
"Egypt does not take Israel's view but it has resorted to the best way by which the parties can return to negotiations and reach agreement, and this is very useful," Netanyahu said.
"We are trying to renew the peace agreements. But we need two to tango," Netanyahu said.
